title: Tantrasāra, Ahnika 2 — The Way with No Way
author: Abhinavagupta
text:
The second ahnika of Abhinavagupta's Tantrasāra continues the work begun in the first: having invoked the divine parents and established the mode of daily recitation, it turns to the way that has no way. When grace has struck firm, the verses hold, one does not fumble for methods — the practice becomes the spontaneous overflow of a recognition already secured, and the texts that prescribe steps are read as descriptions of that overflow rather than as forced labor.

Its juice: this is the tradition's characteristic move, made with full technical backing: method is real, and it is meant to exhaust itself. The second ahnika's juice is its quiet instruction to stop clutching the map — not in favor of carelessness, but in favor of the condition the map was always trying to reach.
